findings.title: wp2shell: Pre Authentication RCE in WordPress Core
findings.summary_md: Searchlight Cyber researcher Adam Kues disclosed the pre-authentication RCE on July 17, 2026, noting it needs no preconditions and works against a stock WordPress install with no plugins, in an ecosystem estimated at over 500 million WordPress sites. Affected branches are 6.9.0 through 6.9.4 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.1, with versions at or below 6.8.5 not affected; the recommended fix is 7.0.2 or 6.9.5, and the interim mitigation is blocking /wp-json/batch/v1 and ?rest_route=/batch/v1 at a WAF. The team also released wp2shell.com as a public exposure-check tool and withheld technical details to give defenders patch time.

findings.title: WordPress 7.0.2 Release
findings.summary_md: The vendor shipped the 7.0.2 security release on July 17, 2026, fixing one critical and one high severity issue and enabling forced auto-updates for affected versions. It credits Adam Kues at Assetnote / Searchlight Cyber for the REST API batch-route confusion and SQL injection leading to RCE, and TF1T, dtro, and haongo for the facilitated SQL injection. Backports fixed both vulnerabilities in 6.9.5 and the 7.1 beta in 7.1 beta2, while 6.8.6 fixes the first vulnerability only; the release lists CVE-2026-60137 / GHSA-fpp7-x2x2-2mjf and CVE-2026-63030 / GHSA-ff9f-jf42-662q.

findings.title: CVE-2026-63030: wp2shell a Critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in WordPress Core
findings.summary_md: Rapid7's Emergent Threat Response post, initially published July 17, 2026 and updated July 22, explains the chain: a logic flaw in the REST API batch processor at /wp-json/batch/v1 desynchronizes validation and execution arrays, which lets CVE-2026-60137's SQL injection in the author__not_in parameter of the posts endpoint bypass parameter validation, ultimately creating an administrator account and uploading a malicious plugin. It carries a CVSS 7.5 score per the advisory and reports that both CVEs were added to CISA's KEV catalog on July 21 with public proof-of-concept exploits circulating. Cloudflare reported the vulnerable code path is reachable when a persistent object cache is not in use, and Rapid7 recommends reviewing HTTP access logs for anomalous batch endpoint requests and unfamiliar plugins or PHP files.

findings.title: WaterPlum threat research overview (NTT Security Japan technical blog)
findings.summary_md: Four days before the Independent piece, NTT Security Japan published an index of its WaterPlum research, linking its four published technical posts on the malware used by the Contagious Interview actors: OtterCookie and its function additions, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle. The post is dated 2026.9.18 on the page.

findings.title: Contagious Interview Campaign Compromises 30,000 Devices, Steals $10.71M in Crypto
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on September 21, 2026 that WaterPlum/Contagious Interview actors compromised at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries and siphoned funds or credentials from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets, at least $10.71 million in total, citing a joint advisory from agencies in Japan, the U.S., Australia, and Germany published at ic3.gov/CSA/2026/260918.pdf. The piece enumerates the campaign's malware families, including BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, FlexibleFerret, GolangGhost, PylangGhost, OtterCookie, RATatouille, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle, and notes a laptop farm operated by a facilitator in Japan was dismantled. It also covers Silent Push's finding of proxy hiring through a Discord server named Mouse Review offering facilitators $3,000 to $5,000 per landed job.

findings.title: Joint cybersecurity advisory on the North Korean fake-recruiter campaign (260918.pdf)
findings.summary_md: The FBI's IC3 hosts the joint cybersecurity advisory on WaterPlum/Contagious Interview, dated September 18, 2026 per its canonical 260918 CSA URL, issued by agencies from Japan, the United States, Australia, and Germany. As reported by The Hacker News, the advisory documents at least 30,000 compromised devices in over 100 countries, more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets drained, and at least $10.71 million stolen, and states some WaterPlum actors also operate as North Korean IT workers, with a laptop farm in Japan identified and dismantled.
